statement: In the square graph with iid edge weights uniform on {1,2}, conditioning on selection of the upper minimum-weight path (ties upper) makes its two edge costs dependent: P(both=2 | selected)=1/11 but the product of marginal probabilities is 16/121; covariance is -5/121. The unconditioned successive selected costs also have covariance -9/256.
assumptions: Two paths between opposite corners of one square; each has two edges
proof_or_counterexample: Exact enumeration of 16 equiprobable assignments; conditional counts 4,3,3,1 and selected joint counts 7,4,4,1.
remaining_gap: No infinite-lattice variance exponent follows; the discrete claim has an independent arithmetic check.

statement: On a square with four iid Exp(1) edges, the two upper-path edge costs have covariance -1/64 conditional on that path being strictly faster. The selected path is unique almost surely.
assumptions: Two simple square paths between opposite corners
proof_or_counterexample: Conditional joint density 2 exp(-2(x+y))(1+x+y); means 5/8 and product moment 3/8 give covariance -1/64.
remaining_gap: Independent check of the continuous control; no asymptotic conclusion.

statement: For finite-graph iid Uniform[1,2] FPP, the clipped off-edge threshold a_e gives centered coordinate response h_a(U)=min(U,a)-a+a^2/2. For 0<=a<=b<=1, its covariance kernel is K(a,b)=a^2[b(2-b)/4-a/6]. With independent rate-one coordinate refresh, Var(T)=integral exp(-t) sum_e E K(a_e(eta),a_e(eta^t)) dt.
assumptions: Finite connected graph and distinct fixed terminals
Off-edge and edge refresh flags are independent; retention probability exp(-t)

statement: For the kernel in C003, H(t)=sum_e E K(a_e(eta),a_e(eta^t)) has a persistent first-order limit L=sum_e ||T_{e}||_2^2, and H(t)-L=sum_{|S|>=2}|S| exp(-(|S|-1)t)||T_S||_2^2. A full-kernel upper bound H(t)<=C n F(n^(1/3)t) for all t>=0 with integrable nonnegative F is impossible when L>0.
assumptions: Hoeffding projections T_S with averaging over each independent coordinate
For the impossible-bound assertion, fixed n,C>0 and L>0
proof_or_counterexample: The finite spectral sum separates |S|=1 exactly. H>=L forces F(s)>=L/(Cn) for all s, contradicting integrability. Exact binary-square check has L=1/4, H(t)=1/4+(3/16)exp(-t)+(1/16)exp(-3t).
remaining_gap: Referee check of the plateau correction and its use in the sufficient route; full exponent untouched.
